sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB / NH-4 / CR / 11 / 2009-10 dated 02.06.2023 pertaining to Sy. No. 11/1A/1A/1A measuring 4425 Sq. feet (411 Sq. Meters) of Makali village, Dasanapura Hobli.

. The definite case of the petitioner is that the property of respondent No.1 measuring 4425 Sq. feet (411 Sq. Meters) in Sy. No. 11/1A/1A/1A of Makali village, Dasanapura Hobli has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 08.02.2008 and Final Notification dated 03.02.2009.

The respondent No.2 has passed the award on 10.06.2009 and determined the market value of agricultural land at Rs.1,50,00,000/- per acre and Rs. 522/- per Sq. feet in respect of non-agricultural land and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.15,22,200/-, which has been received by the respondent No.1 under protest.
Subsequently, on 22.09.2009 the respondent No.1 has filed the application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per Sq. feet.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

sentences.text: .11. The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No. 2 without considering the relevant provisions of NHA Act and also without considering the guidance value or market value of the property as on the date of Preliminary Notification enhanced the compensation by relying on the guidance value of the year 2007 published vide notification bearing No. CVC/BUD/5/2006-07 dated 17.04.2007.
The petitioner also claimed that the Preliminary Notification was published as on 08.02.2008.

As such,
A.P. No.31/2023 the respondent No. 2 ought to have considered the market value of the property of the year 2006 and not of the year 2007.
As the aforesaid notification relied by the Arbitrator came to effect from 17.04.2007 i.e., after lapse of more than 9 months from the date of publication of Preliminary Notification.
Accordingly claimed that the said enhancement cannot be accepted.
It is true that as per the NH Act, the market value of the land as on the date of Preliminary Notification has to be considered.

.12. The petitioner also claimed that whatever the document relied by the respondent No. 2 for enhancing the compensation is not brought to the notice of the petitioner before passing the award/judgment.
Accordingly, claimed that such award is liable to be set aside as per Section 24 of National Highways Authority Act.

In this context, the petitioner relied on the decision reported in (2019) 15 SCC 131 in a case of Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs.
National Highways Authority of India.

sentences.text: It is true that in A.P. No.31/2023 the said decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that whatever the document relied by the Arbitrator shall be brought to the notice of the parties, so that the parties can make submission or give a rebuttal evidence about such documents.
However, in the case on hand, such notification is not found in the record received from the Arbitrator.

.13. In the case on hand, the respondent No.1 claimed that proper award has been passed and no such case has been made out by the petitioner to intervene with the award passed by the respondent No.
2.

When the respondent No. 2 claimed that the respondent No. 2 has passed the order or order is not in accordance with law, then it is for the respondent No. 1 to show that the order passed by the respondent No. 2 is in accordance with law and said order has been passed by following all procedure contemplated under law.

.14. Admittedly, the respondent No. 2 has enhanced the compensation from Rs. 344/- to Rs. Rs.
A.P. No.31/2023 962/- per Sq. feet, which is almost 75% of the market value determined by the LAO.

Hence, it is for the respondent No. 1 to substantiate the fact that the market value of the National Highways Authority Of India vs H C Bhairegowda on 6 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197009888/

sentences.text: 5 acquired property is Rs. 962/- per Sq. feet and not Rs. 344/- per Sq. feet or it is for the petitioner to show that by considering the relevant documents, the respondent No. 2 enhanced the market value of the acquired property and thereby awarded compensation.

.15. It is the claim of the petitioner in the petition that as per the Special Instructions to the notification dated 17.04.2007, it provides that the properties adjacent to National and State Highways for which rates have not been fixed in the rate list, additional rate of 60%, 50% and 25%
of other properties shall be fixed respectively and claimed that if the rate is not fixed for the properties adjacent to the properties of National Highways, the Arbitrator can enhance the price at 50% and in case of State Highways, additional rate of 25% can be fixed.
But 75% cannot be enhanced.

The claim A.P. No.31/2023 of the petitioner is that the Arbitrator / respondent No. 2 enhanced 75% of the market value, which is permissible and accordingly claimed that the enhancement cannot be accepted.
Admittedly, the SLAO fixed the market value to the acquired property is Rs. 344/- and that has been enhanced to Rs. 962/- per Sq. feet.
If the said enhancement is accepted, certainly it is clear that the respondent No. 2 enhanced the market value to the tune of 75%.
Hence, it is for the Arbitrator to give explanation on what basis 75% of the market value has been enhanced.
.16. The only reason assigned by the respondent No. 2 for enhancement of 75% is the discretion.
But it is well settled principle of law that discretion must be used in judiciary or not arbitrary.

Admittedly as observed by the respondent No. 2 in its order as well as claimed by the petitioner in the petition that the Arbitrator can enhance 50% of the market value, if the market value of the acquired property besides National Highways is not found in or fixed in the rate list.
As such, only 50% of A.P. No.31/2023 the market value can be enhanced by the SLAO and not more than that.
If at all the Arbitrator is enhancing another 25%, that is totally 75%, then there must be special reason why the Arbitrator is enhancing 25% of the market value.
Such reasons are not found in the order of the Arbitrator / respondent No. 2.
When such a case, certainly said enhancement cannot be accepted.

It is also not made out by the respondent No. 2 in its order that the property of respondent No. 1 has been acquired, has not found in the rate list, as such, the Arbitrator has added additional rate of 50% along with 25%.
Further the value of the property has been enhanced as per the notification of the year 2007, which is also not the part of records received from the Arbitrator.
Further, no such case is made out by the respondent No. 1 before the respondent No. 2 in the Arbitration proceedings.

Therefore, it is clear that the award passed by the Arbitrator is patently illegal and against the statutory provisions of Substantive Law that is in force and the award passed by the Arbitrator also A.P. No.31/2023 leads to draw adverse inference under Section 24 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act as the documents relied by the Arbitrator not found in the records received from the Arbitrator.

The Arbitrator relied on the guidance value of the year 2007 that came to effect from 01.04.2007 and the land involved in this acquired one year prior to the said date and also the Arbitrator has not given any specific reason for enhancement of 25% as claimed in the year.
As such, certainly the award passed by the Arbitrator is patently illegal.
It is well settled principle of law that if the award passed by the Arbitrator is patently illegal, then such award should be set aside.

As discussed early, as the respondent No. 1 though supported the award passed by the Arbitrator /
respondent No. 2 has not placed any materials to substantiate enhancement made by the Arbitrator to the acquired property.

Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made National Highways Authority Of India vs H C Bhairegowda on 6 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197009888/
6 out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the A.P. No.31/2023 Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.
